ISI Inspection Reports
The Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) visited Sacred Heart School in March 2025 and has published an overwhelmingly positive report. We are thrilled that the report shows that our school has ‘met’ all the Independent School Standards and reflects the outstanding experience our pupils receive in all areas of school life.
The school was inspected under the ISI’s updated framework which evaluates the school across 5 areas. Under this new framework, overall judgements or grades are no longer provided. During their three days, inspectors analysed survey responses; they examined the school’s curriculum, an extensive range of documentation and samples of pupils’ work; they observed many lessons and extra-curricular activities; they attended meetings, registration and assemblies; and they interviewed children, staff and governors.
The success of this inspection was firmly rooted in the excellent work I see here every day. At Sacred Heart School, each child is loved, nurtured and celebrated as an individual. Our children academically excel, they feel safe and supported, and they grow to be the best versions of themselves. I am proud of every single child. My heartfelt thanks go to our inspirational staff whose dedication is reflected across this report, to our parents for all their support, and to our outstanding pupils who embody our school mission statement of Love, Learn, Grow and Worship, ensuring that our school is a happy place to be.
Below are some highlights of our report in each area:
Leadership and Management, and Governance
Governors and leaders “place pupils’ wellbeing at the heart of their practice and decision making. Leaders develop nurturing relationships with pupils so that pupils feel valued and connect to the school.”
“They recognise each pupil as an individual which positively impacts pupils’ self-worth, confidence and readiness to learn.”
Quality of Education, Training and Recreation
“Pupils progress rapidly with their learning as they advance through the school.”
“Lessons involve pupils being stretched to challenge their thinking and deepen their understanding as fully as possible. This is particularly the case within mathematics lessons and when pupils are writing to a high standard.”
“There is an overall atmosphere of calm, purposeful learning in lessons, with high levels of independence.”
Pupils’ Physical and Mental Health and Emotional Wellbeing
“The Catholic ethos permeates school life. They value every member of the school community by recognising and celebrating their individual achievements.”
“Pupils behave with kindness and respect. Pupils have a well-developed understanding of how to treat each other considerately and show tolerance and inclusion in their interactions.”
“Pupils are kind and respectful in their interactions with others, within an atmosphere of ensuring that everyone feels valued and included.”
Pupils’ Social and Economic Education and Contribution to Society
“Pupils engaged meaningfully with the local community… develop empathy for the wider community, contribute positively and increase their understanding of the importance of service to others.”
“The curriculum prepares pupils thoroughly for the process of applying and transferring to secondary school, with many scholarships gained during these applications.”
The school has a “robust safeguarding culture. Pupils have a well-developed understanding of safeguarding and know how to seek help should the need arise.”
“Pupils benefit from a well-informed staff who consistently act in their best interests.”
Surveys completed during the inspection showed:
100% of parents agreed (77% strongly) that their ‘child is happy at school’
100% of children agreed ‘I am happy at school’
100% of parents agreed (74% strongly) that ‘the school supports my child’s social and emotional development’
100% of children agreed that the ‘school supports my good physical and mental health’

Music
Music is a vibrant, exciting and important part of school life. Class lessons are taught by our specialist music teacher, Mrs Wibberley. Children have many opportunities for music making in and out of school, singing in school choirs (KS1 and KS2 choirs), the Tunbridge Wells Arts Festival, community events such as the late-night Christmas shopping in Wadhurst and entertaining the residents of local nursing homes. Music making is enjoyed from Nursery to Y6 and includes a mixture of traditional, classical and contemporary.
We have several dedicated and sympathetic peripatetic teachers who offer private tuition in piano, violin, voice, flute, clarinet, saxophone, guitar and brass. Our children are encouraged to work towards tangible goals and we enter candidates three times a year for the Associated Board of the Royal Schools of Music (ABRSM) exams which are played at Mayfield School, Mayfield. Music theory is offered as a stand alone session. Recorder Club is a popular choice for many of our pupils, and string pupils are invited to our weekly String Group once they have reached a level of proficiency on their instrument. These music-making groups are an enjoyable and very important part of our young musicians' journey.
The Spring and Autumn term Music Evenings are a popular feature of the school calendar, providing an opportunity for all our young musicians to showcase their talents. Other musical highlights include the Harvest Assembly, Mother's Day Assembly, Christmas Carol Service and the Prizegiving performances.
Sacred Heart children are able to develop their acting, singing and performance skills throughout their KS2 journey as we put on two musical productions a year. In February, children in Y3 and Y4 put on a musical and our end-of-year Y5 and Y6 summer musical is a highlight of the school calendar - an experience that the children anticipate eagerly and remember fondly.
Pupils who display a particular musical talent may be encouraged to try for a Music or Choral Scholarship at one of the independent secondary schools. Pupils are regularly successful in this field with awards to Claremont, Westminster, Beechwood and Mayfield being offered in recent years.
We are a proudly and joyously singing school! Hymn singing and group sing-alongs take place weekly. 'To sing is to pray twice': we do so often and with enthusiasm!

Admissions
The written word is no substitute for a visit to the school and we encourage parents to make this a priority when considering a place for their child.
A visit offers you the opportunity to see the school in session on a typical day during a tour with the Head Teacher; to chat to current pupils and staff and to judge for yourself the quality of teaching, learning and relationships within the school.
Following a visit the next step is a 'taster day' which is an opportunity for prospective pupils to discover at first hand what life at Sacred Heart School is really like and for us to assess informally how your child will settle into the school community.
Following the taster day we may make a firm offer. If you feel that Sacred Heart is the right school for your child, registration is the next step to secure your child's place.
Please contact the School Office on 01892 783414 or email admin@sacredheartwadhurst.org.uk for further information.
During the school holiday period and out of school hours please leave a message if the office is unmanned. This facility will be checked regularly and your call returned promptly.
Please refer to the Admissions Policy for further information. This policy can be found on the Policies page of this website.

Celebrating our latest excellent ISI Inspection Report
We are thrilled to share with you, the excellent ISI report that has been written following our inspection at the end of March 2025.
The school was inspected under the ISI’s updated framework which evaluates the school across 5 areas. Under this new framework, overall judgements or grades are no longer provided. During their three days, inspectors analysed survey responses; they examined the school’s curriculum, an extensive range of documentation and samples of pupils’ work; they observed many lessons and extra-curricular activities; they attended meetings, registration and assemblies; and they interviewed children, staff and governors.
The success of this inspection was firmly rooted in the excellent work I see here every day. At Sacred Heart School, each child is loved, nurtured and celebrated as an individual. Our children academically excel, they feel safe and supported, and they grow to be the best versions of themselves. I am proud of every single child.
My heartfelt thanks go to our inspirational staff whose dedication is reflected across this report, to our parents for all their support, and to our outstanding pupils who embody our school mission statement of Love, Learn, Grow and Worship, ensuring that our school is a happy place to be.
We have collated below what we feel are some key observations in the report and in bold are the statements we feel are particularly special.
Jo Collyer Head Teacher

Leaders develop nurturing relationships with pupils so that pupils feel valued and connect to the school. These enable them to acquire new skills in enjoyable ways.”
Quality of Education, Training and Recreation • “Teachers have high expectations for pupils' academic development.” • “Pupils experience a holistic education.” • “Pupils enjoy their learning.” • “The curriculum is flexible so that they can consider the needs and aptitudes of each cohort and adapt the curriculum accordingly.” • “Pupils progress rapidly with their learning as they advance through the school.” • “Lessons involve pupils being stretched to challenge their thinking and deepen their understanding as fully as possible. This is particularly the case within mathematics lessons and when pupils are writing to a high standard.” • “Teachers plan interesting lessons that motivate pupils to work hard and persevere. There is an overall atmosphere of calm, purposeful learning in lessons, with high levels of independence.” • “They are effective at supporting pupils with a variety of learning needs and provide a nurturing approach in their support.” • “Pupils have a well-developed understanding of how they can improve their own learning… as a result of constructive feedback and personalised targets.” • “Teachers in the early years plan topics based on the needs and interests of the children and ensure the children have access to a wide range of activities.”
Pupils’ Physical and Mental Health and Emotional Wellbeing • “The Catholic ethos permeates school life. They value every member of the school community by recognising and celebrating their individual achievements.” • “The Catholic teaching and ethos of the school enable pupils to develop their spiritual and moral understanding.” • “Pupils behave with kindness and respect. Pupils have a well-developed understanding of how to treat each other considerately and show tolerance and inclusion in their interactions.” • Assemblies “teach pupils to be kind and loving towards each other.” • “Develops their ability to show sympathy and empathy to people within their own lives and display a nurturing attitude towards other.” • “All Year 6 pupils have a position of responsibility… these activities develop pupils’ selfesteem through being role models for younger pupils and feeling an integral part of school life.” • “Pupils are kind and respectful in their interactions with others, within an atmosphere of ensuring that everyone feels valued and included.” • “Bullying is rare but is effectively resolved when it does arise.”

Welcome to Sacred Heart School
Welcome to Sacred Heart School and Nursery
We are a small, thriving Catholic independent school for children aged 2–11, where every child is known, valued and supported. Our community is built on warmth, high expectations and a deep sense of care, and we encourage you to visit and experience the school first-hand.
Founded in 1938 by the Sisters of the Order of Notre Dame, Sacred Heart has grown from just 11 pupils to a close-knit, one-form entry school of around 150 children. While much has changed over time, our purpose has remained constant: to provide an excellent education rooted in strong values and a clear sense of mission. With small class sizes, we know each child individually, recognise their unique gifts and talents, and nurture a strong sense of self-worth and aspiration.
At the heart of our school is our mission statement: Love, Learn, Grow, Worship. This is not simply something we say, but something we live each day. Visitors frequently comment on the calm, happy atmosphere of the school, and our children themselves most often describe Sacred Heart in terms of kindness, friendship and love.
We provide high-quality teaching and learning, underpinned by consistently high expectations for every child. Pupils achieve strong academic outcomes and are well prepared for the next stage of their education, with many securing places at their first-choice schools, including success in the 11+ and independent school scholarships.
Alongside this, we are equally committed to the wider development of every child. Our pupils enjoy a rich and varied curriculum and are encouraged to develop confidence, curiosity and resilience. We are proud not only of what they achieve, but of who they become: thoughtful, compassionate and capable young people who are ready to contribute positively to the world around them.
We would be delighted to welcome you to visit Sacred Heart School and Little Hearts Nursery and to see our community in action.
Johanna Collyer MA; PGCE

Catholic Life and Ethos
“The Catholic ethos permeates school life. They value every member of the school community by recognising and celebrating their individual achievements.” ISI Inspection Report 2025
Sacred Heart School was established in 1938 by the Sisters of the Order of Notre Dame to provide an education to the children of local Catholic families. The original school was a brick building and initially accommodated 11 children: the entire school!
The tradition of a small school where everyone is known and valued continues today, although the original building gave way to the new school hall in 2008 and the school has grown steadily to its current status of one form entry from Nursery (2 years old) through to Year 6, with pupil numbers around 150.
The purpose of the school remains steadfast: to provide an excellent education within the mission of the Catholic Church. This does not mean that we are seeking to convert! Rather we encourage each child to think for themselves, to discern what is right and what is wrong, to acknowledge their mistakes, seek forgiveness and in turn to forgive. Every day we strive to be the best that we can be - at school, at home, at work and at play.
Our Catholic life and ethos is not an add-on, taught discretely in RE lessons; rather it is something which is evident in our relationships, and is woven intrinsically through everything that we do.
The whole school comes together on Monday mornings to listen to the Gospel and reflect on God's message for each one of us today. Children are encouraged to develop a personal relationship with Jesus through listening to the gospel, through prayer, through acts of charity. All the children participate in whole school masses and liturgies. We are inclusive and welcoming of children of all faiths and none but we do expect families to be supportive and respectful of our ethos. We would not be the school we are, were we not a Catholic school.
We are a diocesan school, fully supported by the Diocese of Arundel and Brighton and have close relationships with the Sacred Heart parish, situated as we are, adjacent to each other.

pageCache.pageTitle: Celebration of the Word | Sacred Heart School
pageCache.text:
Celebration of the Word
Catholic Life and Ethos
Celebration of the Word
The Feast of St Peter and St Paul
In Matthew’s Gospel, Jesus asks His disciples an important question: "Who do you say I am?" Peter answers with great faith and speaks from his heart, saying, "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God." Jesus is delighted because Peter, who had often made mistakes in the past, trusted God and spoke the truth. Because Jesus knows what is in Peter’s heart, he chooses Peter to be the rock on which He will build His Church.
Jesus doesn’t always choose the people you think he might to lead his Church. Peter and Paul had made bad choices in the past, but Jesus could see in their hearts how much love for Him there was. The most important thing to Jesus is not being perfect but about how much we love him. Jesus knows we sometimes make wrong choices but he looks in our hearts and he chooses people who love him to lead his church, people like Peter and Paul. And here is the amazing thing, he wants to choose us too!
Just like Peter, we are all invited to know Jesus personally and to have the courage to tell others about Him. Sometimes it can feel difficult to stand up for what is right or to say we believe in Jesus, but He promises to help us. We can all be "rocks" by showing kindness, telling the truth, helping others and living as Jesus teaches every day.
12th Sunday in Ordinary Time
This week, Jesus reminds us just how much God loves and cares for each one of us. As Jesus prepares to send his disciples out to share the Good News, he knows that they are worried and afraid. He tells them not to be afraid because God watches over them with great love.
Jesus speaks about the sparrows, explaining that not even one small bird is forgotten by God. He then tells his disciples that even the hairs on their heads are counted. Through these words, Jesus reminds us that we are precious to God and that he knows and loves each one of us completely.
During our prayer together, we reflected on any worries or fears that we may be carrying and remembered that God is always with us. We thought about how much it means to know that we are loved, cared for and never alone.
11th Sunday in Ordinary Time
Following on from our special liturgy to celebrate our Feast Day – the Feast of Sacred Heart - we heard that Jesus loves everyone very much. His Sacred Heart is full of love, so much so that it is shown as burning with love. This reminds us that Jesus cares for every single person.
In Matthew’s Gospel today, Jesus sees people who are lonely, sick, tired, or sad, and he feels compassion. Compassion means caring so much about someone that you want to help them. Sometimes we feel compassion too. When we see someone who needs help and want to be kind to them, that loving feeling comes from Jesus working in our hearts. Jesus chose 12 special friends, called disciples, to help him share his love with others. He called each one by name because each person was important to him. Jesus sent his friends to help people who were hurting and to show them God's love. He told them to be kind, heal people, and help others without expecting anything in return.
Jesus loves us too, and he calls us by name. He wants us to share his love with our family, friends, and everyone we meet. During prayer, we can ask Jesus to show us who needs our kindness and how we can share the love of his Sacred Heart.
The Feast of The Sacred Heart of Jesus
We began our special feast day with a whole school liturgy which was focused on the meaning of the Sacred Heart of Jesus and why our school name is so special. The image of the Sacred Heart, with flames surrounding it and displayed outside Jesus’ body, represents a heart burning with love and open to all people. Jesus points to His heart as a sign that He freely gives His love and kindness to everyone.
Each year group took part with the Nursery setting up the prayer focus and leading us in the singing of "Come and Join the Circle". Other year groups read from Scripture; they recited a psalm and a poem and led us in prayer. Reception Class gave us some beautiful examples of why they love Sacred Heart School and Year One shared with us some joyful ways that we show love in our special school.
All the children sang hymns so beautifully and we were very proud of them. It was wonderful to welcome so many parents who were able to join us for this special liturgy, helping us celebrate the fact that we are all part of one big Sacred Heart Family.
Corpus Christi
This week was the Solemnity of Corpus Christi, a special feast that celebrates Jesus' gift of Himself in the Eucharist.
Through the Gospel of John (6:51–58), we reflected on Jesus' words: "I am the living bread that came down from heaven." We explored how Jesus invites us to trust in Him and recognise His presence in the bread and wine that become His Body and Blood at Mass.
Children were encouraged to think about the disciples who remained faithful to Jesus, even when His teaching was difficult to understand, and to reflect on the great gift of the Eucharist. Through prayer and quiet reflection, we thanked Jesus for His love, His presence in our lives, and for remaining with us through the Blessed Sacrament.
Children were invited to write their own prayers of thanksgiving, expressing gratitude to God for His many gifts and blessings.
The Solemnity of The Most Holy Trinity
In our Celebration of the Word assembly, we heard about how our God is three persons in one: God the Father, God the Son (Jesus) and God the Holy Spirit. Although it is a mystery, we can think of the Trinity as a Family of Love.
The Father loves the Son, the Son loves the Father, and the Holy Spirit is the love that flows between them. They are perfectly united, always giving and receiving love. Because God loves us so much, He invites us to be part of this family of love.
In John’s Gospel this week, we hear Jesus tell us that God loves us more than we can imagine: "God loved the world so much that He gave His only Son." Jesus explains that God the Father sent Him into the world, not to punish people, but to save them. God wants everyone to know His love and to be close to Him forever. Jesus came to show us how much God cares for us and to help us find our way to Him.
This Gospel reminds us that God's love is a gift for everyone. No matter who we are, God loves us and wants us to trust in Him. The Holy Trinity shows us that love is at the heart of who God is, and He wants us to fill our homes, schools, and friendships with that same love.
The Seventh Sunday of Easter: The Ascension of the Lord
Jesus meets His disciples one last time on a mountain. When they see Him, they worship Him because they know He is holy and full of God’s power. Jesus tells them that all authority in Heaven and on earth has been given to Him. He sends them out to share His love with all nations and to baptise people in the name of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit.
Jesus knows this mission will feel big and difficult, so He makes them a beautiful promise: “I am with you always.”
Then Jesus ascends into Heaven.
Even though the disciples cannot see Jesus anymore, they know He is still close to them. Jesus promises to send the Holy Spirit to help them. The disciples leave the mountain trusting in His promise and waiting in prayer.
We can trust this promise too. Jesus is always with us. He sees us, loves us, hears our prayers and stays close to us every day.
The Sixth Sunday of Easter
The Fourth Sunday of Easter - Good Shepherd Sunday
In this Sunday’s Gospel from the Gospel of John, Jesus describes himself as the Good Shepherd who cares for his sheep. A shepherd knows each of his sheep, calls them by name, and keeps them safe. The sheep listen to his voice and follow him because they trust him.
Jesus tells us that he knows each one of us and loves us deeply. He guides us, protects us, and shows us the right way to live. He also says that he has come so that we may have life to the full: a life filled with love, peace, and joy.
This Gospel reminds us how important it is to listen carefully for Jesus’ voice in our lives. Sometimes there are many voices around us, but Jesus leads us towards kindness, goodness, and truth.
Good Shepherd Sunday helps us to remember that we are never alone. Jesus is always with us, guiding us and caring for us. When we follow him, we learn how to love others and live as he teaches us.
The Third Sunday of Easter
In this Sunday’s Gospel from the Gospel of Luke, we hear the story of two disciples walking to a place called Emmaus. They are feeling sad and confused after everything that has happened to Jesus. As they walk, Jesus comes and joins them, but they do not recognise him at first.
Jesus walks with them, listens to them, and explains the Scriptures. Slowly, their sadness begins to turn into hope, and their hearts feel full and alive. Later, when they sit down to eat, Jesus takes bread, blesses it, breaks it, and gives it to them. In that moment, they recognise him and realise that Jesus has been with them all along.
The disciples are so filled with joy that they hurry back to share the Good News: Jesus is alive!
This Gospel reminds us that Jesus is always with us, even when we don’t realise it. We can recognise him in special moments: in prayer, in scripture, in the breaking of the bread, and in the people around us. As we continue through the season of Easter, we are reminded to walk with Jesus and share his joy with others.
The Fifth Sunday of Lent
As we come to the end of Lent, we begin to look forward to Holy Week and the great joy of Easter. In this Sunday’s Gospel from the Gospel of John, we hear the powerful story of Jesus raising his friend Lazarus from the dead. This story reminds us that even in the saddest times, Jesus brings hope and new life.
Jesus travels to the village of Bethany to be with his friends Mary and Martha after their brother Lazarus has died. They are very upset, and when Jesus sees their sadness, he is deeply moved and even cries. This shows us that Jesus cares about us and shares in our pain when we are sad or hurting.
Jesus tells Martha, “I am the resurrection and the life,” and makes an amazing promise that those who believe in him will live forever. This reminds us that death is not the end, but the beginning of new life with God.
At the tomb, Jesus calls out, “Lazarus, come out,” and Lazarus walks out alive. Imagine how everyone must have felt seeing this miracle! This shows that Jesus has power over everything, even death, and that nothing is impossible for him.
Some people who saw this miracle began to believe in Jesus, while others struggled to understand. This reminds us that faith can grow, just like in other Gospel stories, as we learn to trust more and more in Jesus.
This Gospel teaches us that Jesus is always with us, especially in times of sadness. He brings comfort, hope and the promise of new life. As we prepare for Easter, we remember that Jesus’ love is stronger than anything.
The Fourth Sunday of Lent – Laetare Sunday
Laetare Sunday comes in the middle of Lent and reminds us that joy and hope are coming because Easter is near. We meet Jesus in John’s Gospel when we hear about the story of Jesus healing a man who had been blind since he was born. This story teaches us an important lesson about learning to see not only with our eyes but also with our hearts.
In the story, Jesus heals the blind man and he is finally able to see the world around him. Imagine the joy he must have felt! This shows that Jesus is like a light that helps people who are in darkness. The miracle is not only about the man’s eyes being healed, but also about understanding who Jesus really is.
As the story continues, the man begins to believe more and more in Jesus. At first, he only knows that Jesus healed him. Later, he understands that Jesus comes from God. Finally, he believes in Jesus completely. This shows that faith can grow step by step, just like learning something new.
Sadly, the religious leaders in the story could see with their eyes, but they refused to believe in Jesus. Even though their eyes worked, their hearts were closed. They are blinded by jealousy, anger and hatred. This teaches us that real blindness can happen when people refuse to see the truth or ignore God.
The Gospel reminds us that Christ is the Light who helps us to see fully. We should try to see with our eyes and our hearts. Seeing with our eyes means noticing people around us - especially those who need help or kindness. Seeing with our hearts means loving others, believing in God, and recognizing the good things Jesus does in our lives.
Laetare Sunday teaches us that Jesus is the light who helps us see clearly. When we follow Him, we learn to look at the world with kindness, faith, and love.
The Third Sunday of Lent – The Woman at the Well
In our Celebration of the Word this week, we heard the Gospel story of when Jesus met a Samaritan woman at a well. The woman came to the well during the hottest part of the day because she was trying to avoid other people. She felt ashamed and believed she was not worthy to be accepted.
Even though people in those days believed she was “unclean”, Jesus spoke to her with kindness and asked her for a drink. He told her that He could offer her “living water” - a gift that would never run out. Jesus was speaking about God’s love and the Holy Spirit, which fills our hearts and gives us new life.
Through this encounter, the woman realised that Jesus was the Messiah. She ran back to her town to tell everyone about Him, sharing the good news with those she had once tried to avoid.
This Gospel reminds us that Jesus loves every person and meets us wherever we are in our lives. No matter what others may say about us, or what mistakes we may have made, Jesus always reaches out to us and invites us into a relationship with Him.
During Lent, we are encouraged to grow closer to Jesus through prayer allowing us

Prayer Bear
Catholic Life and Ethos
Prayer Bear
Meet our Prayer Bear!
The Prayer Bear is something we are introducing at school to help children develop their prayer life.
We would like to encourage children to:
Our Prayer Bear is a soft, cuddly toy who takes turns in coming home with your child if they have asked for him. Inside the Prayer Bear bag, you will find traditional prayers, prayer starters, prayer artefacts and some suggestions for how you might like to share some prayers at home as a family.
There is no right or wrong way to use the Prayer Bear!
There is also a small prayer book with space for children and families to add their own prayers, drawings or photographs.
When Prayer Bear comes back to school, we will share some of the children’s reflections during Prayer & Liturgy. This helps children see that their prayers at home are part of our wider school family’s prayer life.
Our hope is that through Prayer Bear, we hope children and families will grow closer to God, find comfort in prayer, and feel connected to the faith community of Sacred Heart School.
What’s inside the bag?
How to use a Prayer Bear
1. Choose a quiet moment in the day (morning, afternoon, evening or whenever works best)
2. Switch on the tea light and invite your child to hold the cross and the Prayer Bear
3. Say a prayer together – you can choose one from the selection in the bag or choose your own prayer to say, use the prayer starters or just talk to God in your own way
4. Write or draw something in the Prayer Journal - it could be a prayer, something you are thankful for or a picture. If you would like to pop a prayer or picture or photo into Prayer Bear’s pocket, please feel free to do so.
5. Return everything back in the bag to school so the next child can take the Prayer Bear home.
Ideas for your prayer time
Thank you for making Prayer Bear’s visit to your home so special.

Mission statement
“Pupils behave with kindness and respect. Pupils have a well-developed understanding of how to treat each other considerately and show tolerance and inclusion in their interactions.” ISI Inspection Report 2025
At Sacred Heart School we all aspire to provide a happy, safe and secure environment in which every child is encouraged to achieve their full potential, within an inclusive community, which is centred on Christ's teachings and shared Gospel values and which affirms the Catholic ethos of the founding religious order of Notre Dame.
We offer a broad, balanced and relevant curriculum that promotes the spiritual, moral, emotional and physical development of each child. We provide high quality teaching and learning opportunities and experiences based on equally high expectations of every child.
We acknowledge the unique gifts of each child and instil a strong sense of self-worth by celebrating personal achievements and strengths. Leading by example we teach children to respect themselves and each other as unique and equally valuable members of God's universal family.
We engage in partnership with parents and parish for the good of every member of the community. Worship and prayer are central to the life of the school and are embedded in the whole curriculum, thus safeguarding, supporting and strengthening the spiritual life of all.

Pupils' Achievements and Destinations
“The curriculum prepares pupils thoroughly for the process of applying and transferring to secondary school, with many scholarships gained during these applications.” ISI Inspection Report 2025
Pupils' Achievements and Destinations
Leavers 2024 - 2025
Our Year 6s leave Sacred Heart to continue their journey at a range of schools, including: Tonbridge Grammar, Weald of Kent Grammar, Mayfield, Worth, Cranbrook Grammar, Dulwich College Cranbrook, Battle Abbey, Lingfield College, Heathfield Community College, Beechwood, Bennett Memorial, and Rose Hill.
Around 40-50% of our Year 6 pupils every year sit the Kent Test and we are thrilled to share that this year, the average score of those who passed was an exceptional 392, far above the pass mark of 332.
We are especially proud of the scholarships awarded in Drama, Music, Hockey, and Academics — a reflection of their talent, dedication, and all-round excellence.
Leavers 2023 - 2024
Our Year 6s have gained places at a range of excellent schools: Tonbridge Grammar School, TWGGS, Mayfield, The Skinners’ School, Tunbridge Wells Boys Grammar School, Battle Abbey, Stamford School, Bennett Memorial School, Uplands, Claremont, and Bethany.
5 children were allocated Grammar Schools.
Scholarships were awarded in Musical Theatre, Design and Technology, an All-rounder scholarship and an unconditional offer to Tonbridge School.
Leavers 2022 - 2023
Congratulations to our Year 6 pupils who gained places at the following schools: The Skinner’s School, Mayfield, Worth School, Queenswood, Cranbrook, Tunbridge Wells Boys Grammar, Weald of Kent Grammar School, Bethany, Northease Manor, Frewen, Heathfield Community College, Bennett Memorial School and Uplands.
5 children were allocated Grammar Schools.
Scholarships were awarded in Sport, Musical Theatre and an unconditional offer to Tonbridge School.
Leavers 2021 - 2022
Our Year 6 pupils had a very successful year. The children performed exceptionally well in their SATs tests and despite being a non-selective school, both Key Stage 1 and Key Stage 2 results were significantly above the national average, with a significant number of children gaining greater depth in each subject area.
Destination of July 2022 leavers
Whilst many of our pupils follow the 11+ route, others have gained places at a range of independent and state schools; schools which allow our pupils to thrive and continue to reach their potential. Destination schools for 2022: Tonbridge School, Tonbridge Grammar School for Girls, Tunbridge Wells Girls' Grammar School, Mayfield, Tunbridge Wells Grammar School for Boys, Skinners Grammar School for Boys, Bennett Memorial School, Rose Hill, and Bethany.
9 children were allocated Grammar Schools.
